candidates.tagline: Samsung's AI fridge plays music, suggests recipes, and ruins Chuseok dinner
candidates.story: A botched SmartThings firmware update on September 22, 2026 bricked Samsung Bespoke AI 4-Door refrigerators across South Korea just days before Chuseok — cooling failed entirely, screens went dark, and owners who paid ~$4,000 for fridges with recipe AI and music playback had to discard holiday food while awaiting in-person technician visits scheduled for after the holiday.
candidates.why_funny: Samsung spent years adding AI, recipe suggestions, and music streaming to a century-old reliable appliance, then a software update stripped out the one thing a fridge absolutely must do: stay cold.
candidates.alt: A Samsung smart refrigerator with a large touchscreen display panel built into the front door, showing the connected-appliance interface that turned a fridge into a software dependency

candidates.tagline: Thieves stole trailers branded with Nvidia. Inside: 20 tons of sand.
candidates.story: On September 24, 2026, thieves stole two trailers from PlusAI's autonomous-trucking warehouse in Fremont, California, drawn by the prominent Nvidia branding and convinced they'd scored a fortune in AI chips; the trailers contained 20 tons of sand used to simulate freight loads during self-driving truck testing — the thieves abandoned both rigs just four miles away.
candidates.why_funny: Slapping the world's hottest AI brand on a truck full of sand fooled actual criminals into committing a heist for construction materials — the most expensive-looking 20 tons of quartz in Silicon Valley.
candidates.alt: A white semi-truck trailer bearing PlusAI and Nvidia co-branding parked in front of a glass office building — the truck the thieves stole, expecting AI hardware
